title: Snyk was worth $8.5 billion. The price of its employees' stock has collapsed.
summary:
Snyk was one of cybersecurity's brightest startup stars, worth $8.5 billion at the height of the software boom.
It was valued at $8.5 billion in a 2021 funding round and at $7.4 billion in a 2022 funding round.
People with Snyk equity have been watching the value of their shares slide over the past few years, two former employees told Business Insider.
Snyk said it doesn't comment on employee share valuations and declined to provide a valuation for Snyk at this time.

title: How to Build a Capital Stack That Gives Your Startup More Control
summary:
Listen to this postKey Takeaways Venture capital is no longer the default startup financing strategy.
Founders should build a diversified capital stack — three sources of capital that each do a different job and don’t depend on the same market conditions being favorable at the same time.
Debt, venture debt, revenue-based financing or asset-backed lending works once you have predictable revenue or hard assets to underwrite against.
Debt, venture debt, revenue-based financing or straightforward asset-backed lending works once you have predictable revenue or hard assets to underwrite against.
Raise venture capital when it buys you something specific, not because it’s the only playbook you were handed.

title: Business Formations Are at Record Highs — and the Fastest-Growing States Aren’t the Ones You’d Guess
summary:
AI, cloud computing and the adoption of remote work have changed the dynamics of starting a business.
Founders no longer need to be in a major civic hub to access trained talent, sophisticated business tools or even global markets.
Now AI allows founders, even solo or two-person ventures, to perform many tasks themselves before making their first hires.
Remote work unchains employees from officesAlong with powerful AI tools, post-COVID remote work has altered another enduring business assumption: that employers and employees must share the same offices.
Entrepreneurs have always been encouraged to “Think differently.” With a leg up from AI and remote work, that mindset is extending into where they plan.
